title: Company winter sprint orchestration and stage directions v0.1
content:
Purpose: Rapid draft for winter company sprint (Feb–Apr), combined all-company meeting flow, and a minimalist OKR seed set we can iterate in Monday syncs. This is a planning artifact not final — use as the single place to collect asks, owners, and stage directions for leadership and comms.

What this doc is NOT: final OKRs, not the polished all-hands slide deck, not a replacement for longer product or SRE plans. It is the orchestration shell — who says what, when, and where dependencies live.

High-level objectives for the quarter (seed, for debate):
- Objective A: Reduce 99th percentile user-facing latency across hosted inference by 20% while reducing per-token cost by 10% for targeted workloads.
  - Key result A1: Deploy new batching/caching control for top-10 enterprise routes; measure cost delta and latency.
  - Key result A2: Roll out optimized kernels for 2 model families on Dedicated; validate latency SLO at >=95% of traffic.
- Objective B: Make Redwood Private onboarding frictionless for midsize customers (trial-to-deploy time <= 6 weeks).
  - Key result B1: Create a 5-step onboarding checklist, automate two setup steps in the console.
  - Key result B2: Pilot with 3 customers and document mean time to first inference.
- Objective C: Improve developer visibility and cost controls across product surface (Console + API) to reduce billing surprises.
  - Key result C1: Add route-level cost breakdown to Console for top 5 paid orgs.
  - Key result C2: Launch an opt-in cost-alert beta for experimental teams.

Notes on KR metrics: these are measurable with existing telemetry (trace samples, token billing exports). If metric instrumenting work > 2 sprints, flag as dependency and re-scope.

All-hands (company meeting) run-of-show draft — 45 minutes total
- 0:00–0:05 — Opening (CEO): quick wins, current topline (usage, high-level revenue highlight) — 1 slide, emotive opener (customer quote or incident averted). Owner: CEO (Marco Chen to prep slide).
- 0:05–0:15 — Product & Tech priorities (VP Product + Head of Serving Runtime): 2 slides — one on customer-facing features (dedicated + private highlights) and one on reliability/cost work (Objective A summary). Owner: Elena Rodriguez.
- 0:15–0:25 — Customer momentum (CS): 1 slide per pilot customer highlight + ask to the org (engineering needs). Owner: Priya Singh.
- 0:25–0:35 — People & org updates (Head of People): hires, open roles, DEI micro-goals. Owner: Devon O'Leary.
- 0:35–0:43 — Ops deep-dive (SRE/Product ops): a single backstage look at a recent improvement (e.g., new routing fallback) + short demo. Owner: SRE lead (TBD).
- 0:43–0:45 — Closing + asks + Slack follow-up thread launch. Owner: Aisha Patel.

Pre-reads (send 72 hours before):
- One-pager: "Winter sprint goals & how you can help" (1 page).
- Short status snapshot: KR health matrix (traffic, latency, onboarding MTTI).
- 3 customer vignettes (one paragraph each) with redacted metrics.
Action: comms to assemble pre-reads: Elena + Priya by 2025-02-10.

Detailed orchestration checklist (people + deadlines):
- By 2025-02-03: Draft one-pager + leadership talking bullets. Owner: Aisha.
- By 2025-02-05: Engineering owners commit to demo scope (if any) and provide 2-minute demo script. Owners: Serving runtime leads.
- By 2025-02-07: Slides first pass. Owner: Design partner (Kate M.).
- By 2025-02-10: Pre-reads posted to Confluence + Slack thread created. Owner: Comms (Elena).
- By 2025-02-12: Rehearsal 30m (leadership + MC). Owner: Aisha.
- On event day: MC to post TL;DR and open Qs doc in Slack. Owner: Aisha.

Runbook: risk register and mitigations (quick):
- Risk: demo fails or feature not ready. Mitigation: prerecorded video + fallback slide. Owner: Serving runtime.
- Risk: metrics look worse than expected. Mitigation: present context, show plan and short-term compensations (rate-limits, routing changes). Owner: Product.
- Risk: overloaded CS asks. Mitigation: triage CS asks to "product ops backlog" and surface top 3 to execs. Owner: CS lead.

OKR process notes (how we will iterate):
- Round 1 (this doc): seed objectives and KRs for leadership review.
- Round 2 (leadership comment): two-week window for rewrite and metric gating.
- Round 3 (public draft): share with managers 1 week before all-hands for team-level alignment.
- Lock: end of first sprint (2025-02-28).

Open questions to resolve in first leadership sync:
- Do we want a separate Customer Day later in the quarter, or fold customer stories into the main all-hands?
- Can Dedicated capacity cadence be accelerated for kernel rollout without breaking existing SLAs? (SRE input required)
- Which 3 customers do we pick for Private pilot material — legal signoff timeline?

Communication tone guidance: candid, operational, low-on-buzzword — focus on what we will measure and who will do the work. Keep the all-hands to 45 minutes; save deeper technical demos for smaller brown-bag sessions.

Draft Slack announcement (short):
Hey everyone — save the date: Winter Sprint kickoff is Feb 15, 10:00 PT. We’ll share a 2-page pre-read 72 hrs prior. Expect a quick 45-minute all-company and a follow-up Q&A thread. Leadership will cover latency/cost work, Private onboarding pilots, and immediate asks where we need help.

Post-event follow-up plan:
- 24 hours: publish TL;DR + link to recording + thread summary. Owner: Aisha.
- 72 hours: collect top-10 action items and owners (auto-generated from Qs doc). Owner: Product Ops.
- End of week: publish KR health snapshot. Owner: Analytics.

Appendix (working notes & fragments):
- Potential quick wins to highlight: improved KV cache hit-rate in beta, one enterprise customer re-sign with 10% more committed spend, a new SLO at 95th token latency.
- Quick TODOs: assign rehearsal roles, pick MC, finalize demo recording platform (Zoom vs Loom).
- Links: Confluence draft space: confluence:COMPANY-WINTER-2025-PLAN; JIRA epic: ORG-3245 (sprint orchestration).

Immediate next steps (today):
- Leadership: read this doc and add one-line comments by EOD Friday (Aisha will collect).
- Product/ENG: identify demo scope and blockers by Monday standup.
- Comms/Design: pick slide template and draft one-pager.

If you want to change the run-of-show or add an ask, add a comment below with suggested owner and deadline. This doc should converge to a single-page runbook with links to the slides and pre-reads 3 days before the meeting.

Quick contact list: Aisha Patel (owner, aisha@redwood.com), Elena Rodriguez (comms), Priya Singh (CS), Devon O'Leary (people ops), Marco Chen (CEO).

-- end of draft v0.1 --
